packages.label: דִּין וְדָמִים וְרַגְלִין
packages.label_en: Judgment, Blood, and Legs — The Din Cycle
packages.reason: All seven nodes share the essential nature of the din-cycle: the metaphysical mechanism by which divine judgment (דין) manifests in the physical body and is ultimately sweetened. The Rebbe explicitly equates: דָּמִים = דִּינִים (blood is a bechina of judgments — the blood that flows into the legs IS the judgments settling there); עִבּוּר = דִּין (pregnancy is a bechina of judgment — 'as a pregnant woman is filled with wrath', Berakhot 29b); לֵדָה = הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּין (childbirth is a bechina of the sweetening of judgment — when birth occurs, the blood/din exits the legs); שְׁלוּחֵי הַדִּין = רַגְלִין (the agents of judgment are called 'runners' in the Zohar, and they are a bechina of legs — the legs are where judgment concentrates). The polarity is neutral because this cluster represents a structural metaphysical mechanism — divine judgment and its biological/bodily correlates — rather than intrinsically good or evil content. The same leg-system that is heavy with din is the one that dances with joy when din is sweetened. The pregnancy-birth metaphor covers both poles (din = gestation, sweetening = delivery) as phases of one cycle, making the cluster structurally bilateral rather than polarity-fixed.
merge_notes: Raw Component A {דין, דם, עבור} (3 nodes): the core bechina hub. דין is the hub with degree 2; דם and עבור each equated directly with דין.

Raw Component B {לדה, המתקת הדינים} (2-node pair): merged here. לדה = המתקת הדין is a direct, explicit bechina. The shared nature with Component A is the din-cycle: עבור IS din (the concentration phase) and לדה IS the sweetening of din (the release phase) — both are facets of the same din-cycle metaphysical structure, not a cause-and-effect relationship between them. The merge is by shared domain: the pregnancy-birth-judgment metaphor is one integrated structure.

Raw Component C {שלוחי הדין, רגלים} (2-node pair): merged here. שלוחי הדין = רגלים by explicit bechina (Zohar Bereshit 43). The shared nature with Component A is direct: the legs ARE where din settles (the blood/din flows to the legs), and the agents of din ARE the legs. This is the same din-body-mechanism that Components A and B describe. Shared nature: the bodily location and physical carrier of din, not a separate thematic domain.
